title: Tier choice is a markdown side effect: make it a gate-first decision in results
premise_notes: Verified: summary.rs:715 carries the selection rule as report prose; summary.rs:754-767 computes the winner inside report_md with judged>0 && rule_fails()==0, ranking by quality then p50 latency, with cost printed but not deciding; CellKey has no judge tier and judge_tiers is merged per cell; CellResult and TournamentResults carry no decision field; registry-map.json:3430 records the deviation at summary.rs:756. One overreach: the claim that 'grep -i winner apps/console/src/pages/simulator finds no match' is false (BandArt.module.css comments mention a design 'winner'). The substantive point, that nothing in the console reads a tier winner, still stands. packages/contract is private:true, so no other repository consumes it.
floor_notes: L/7/8/5, 8 files, 7 cases. Gate architecture with an additive, serde-default change to the in-repo contract. Closes a recorded deviation without restating it.
ambition_why: It turns the tournament's actual answer from report prose into a typed, gate-first decision that conforms to the declared cheapest-passing-tier standard. This is the move the subsystem exists for.
grounding_why: Core claims all hold. The console 'no winner match' grep is literally false, though immaterial.
falsifiability_why: Cases 1, 3 and 5 decide differently from today and are red. But case 5 leaves the 'reference judge tier' undefined, and a cell can hold several judge tiers (judge_tiers is a Vec). Since a sonnet core can never be judged by sonnet, a builder could choose a rule that systematically shunts one tier to beside[] and still pass.
revision: Rewrite acceptance case 5 to pin the rule: the reference judge is the judge tier that judged the most cells in the group (ties go to the higher tier); a cell whose judge_tiers holds more than one tier, or a tier other than the reference, is listed in beside[] with reason judge_mismatch; add the assertion that a group with a single judge tier ranks every cell.
reason: Strong, grounded card whose judge-slice rule is underspecified enough to let a wrong build pass.
